code:
SABSA — built by practitioners, not a standards body
(John Sherwood, Andrew Clark, David Lynas; maintained
by the SABSA Institute)

The core rule:
  A control that can't trace back to a real business
  requirement isn't architecture.
  It's just a control someone liked.
caption: SABSA's whole premise: security has to justify itself in business terms.

eyebrow: Six layers, each one more concrete

steps.label: Physical → Component → Operational
steps.sub: Real tech, real configs, day-to-day running

code:
6 layers x 6 questions = the SABSA Matrix

  What   Why   How   Who   Where   When

asked again at EVERY layer:
  Contextual  -> business asset, business driver...
  Component   -> specific hardware/software setting...

Traceability = answer the same questions, layer by layer.
caption: The matrix isn't filled in cell-by-cell every time — the discipline is what matters.

code:
Built WITH business stakeholders, not IT alone:
  - Regulatory compliance
  - Customer confidence
  - Operational resilience
  - Time to market

Every proposed control must serve a named attribute
— or the profile needs revisiting first.
caption: This profile is the yardstick SABSA measures every control against.
